user.title: Connect to a SAJ inverter
user.description: Enter the local Modbus TCP endpoint, polling interval and model. Leave the model on Automatic unless the inverter is not recognised.

data_description.prefix: Optional. Adds a prefix to this installation's entity IDs, for example sensor.saj_house_pv_power instead of sensor.saj_pv_power. Use it when you have more than one SAJ system. Lowercase letters and digits only, no underscores, up to 32 characters, and no two installations can share one.

confirm_model.title: Confirm model
confirm_model.description: The device reports type {device_type}, which is not recognised as {model}, so it could not be verified as that model. Its required registers answered, but readings may be wrong if it is a different model. Use {model} anyway?

confirm_control.title: Confirm that control is allowed
confirm_control.description:
With control allowed, entity changes and automations will change the settings of your inverter. A wrong setting can stop the inverter, change how it uses the battery or the grid, or cost you money.

Enabling EMS functions disables the inverter's reverse-current protection.

When Home Assistant stops or this installation is reloaded, it tries to switch off the functions you switched on from Home Assistant. This is a best effort, not a guarantee. If the inverter cannot be reached or Home Assistant stops abruptly, they can stay on. The inverter's own EMS timeout may then end them, but it has not proved reliable.

Allow control?

data_description.ems_heartbeat: How often the targets of the EMS functions you switch on from Home Assistant, and the EMS limits, are read to keep them alive, from 30 to 3600 seconds. The inverter's EMS timeout must be longer than this. Shown only for models with EMS.

equipment.name: Equipment
equipment.description: Treated as fitted now: {equipment_fitted}. Automatic detects each at every start and every reload, and keeps what it has detected until you choose Not fitted. Fitted creates its entities without detecting. Not fitted removes its entities from Home Assistant, including any customisations you made to them, and forgets what was detected. Entity IDs stay the same if it is fitted again, so history continues.

data_description.battery: Battery entities. When the inverter does not answer the detection, a battery is assumed.
data_description.meter_a: Entities of the first meter. When the inverter does not answer the detection, the meter is assumed.
data_description.meter_b: Entities of the second meter, detected from the inverter's meter B status.
data_description.ev_charger: Entities of the SAJ EV charger, detected from the inverter's EV charger enable setting.
data_description.parallel: Entities of a parallel machine system, detected from the inverter's parallel mode and the number of machines online.

confirm_prefix.title: Confirm entity ID change
confirm_prefix.description:
Entity IDs change from `{old_pattern}` to `{new_pattern}`, for every entity type.

History and long-term statistics move to the new entity IDs.

Automations, scripts, dashboards, templates and Energy settings that use the old entity IDs will stop working until you update them.

Entities you renamed yourself are left alone. Change the entity IDs?

The integration sends the inverter at most {budget} requests per minute, so that its communication module is not overloaded. Because that is over the limit, entities will be read slower than configured. Save the interval anyway?

user.description: Entities in a polling group are read at the group's own interval. All other entities are read at the default interval. The integration sends the inverter at most {budget} requests per minute, so that its communication module is not overloaded. This installation currently uses {load} of them. user.title: Add power control schedule
user.description: Pick the function to hold at a set power and the Home Assistant schedule helper that says when. The integration switches the function on when the schedule turns on and off when it turns off. A schedule block can carry the additional data power, in whole watts, with a negative number to charge or import and a positive one to discharge or export; without it the function's power target is used. Allow control must be on.

registers_refused.description: The inverter keeps refusing these readings of {installation}, so they are no longer read: {entities}. Check that the inverter and its communication module have power, that the network between Home Assistant and the inverter works, and that no other Modbus client holds the connection. This repair goes away at the first good reading.
